claim: ViralSweep's core product is a self-serve promotions SaaS offering Sweepstakes, Giveaway, Contest (photo/video UGC), and Instant Win apps aimed at growing email/SMS lists and social engagement for brands.
page_title: ViralSweep - Sweepstakes, Giveaways, Contests & Instant Win Platform
notes: Homepage lists Sweepstakes, Giveaway, Contest, Instant Win, Hashtags, Comments, Waitlist, Milestones, Purchases, Email Capture, Gallery apps; claims 'thousands of brands'.

claim: The product suite spans 11 promotion app types (incl. hashtag entries from Instagram/Twitter, Facebook/Instagram/YouTube comment giveaways, waitlist referrals, milestone referral tiers, purchase-to-enter, galleries) delivered as hosted/embedded campaign pages with 60+ email/CRM integrations and e-commerce platform integrations (Shopify, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, Magento).
notes: Embed/hosted-page delivery model; integration breadth is marketing-listed, individual integration docs exist in support center.

claim: Public pricing: Starter $49/mo (1 brand, no extra users), Business $199/mo (white label, custom actions, 2 brands/2 users), Premium $399/mo (API access, A/B testing, audience segments, multiple languages, 4 brands/4 users), Elite $999/mo (white glove service, 1 promotion built monthly, 6 brands/6 users), plus contact-sales Enterprise tier.
page_title: Plans and Pricing (7-Day Free Trial) | Viralsweep
notes: All paid tiers include unlimited promotions and entries; 7-day free trial; annual discount ~17%.

claim: API access requires the Premium plan or higher AND a request to support to enable it; stated use cases are submitting data via custom forms, updating user records on task completion, retrieving entrant info, and applying entries — positioned as letting you 'build, run, and manage your own promotions outside of your platform'.
notes: The 'build, run, manage outside the platform' language overstates the documented endpoint surface (see VIRALSWEEP-005: no campaign-creation endpoints).

claim: The documented API surface is 7 endpoints: GET /api/brands; GET /api/promotions/<BRAND_ID> (optional all/active incl. archived); GET /api/entries/<PROMOTION_ID> (pagination, email query; returns email, timestamps, location, IP, referral info, custom fields); POST /api/entries/<PROMOTION_ID> (add entry); POST /api/points/<PROMOTION_ID> (add/subtract points with description); POST /api/validate/<PROMOTION_ID> (mark entries valid/invalid/accept/unaccept, bulk by email); GET /api/winners/<PROMOTION_ID> (with begin_ts/end_ts filters). Auth is an x-api-key header; JSON responses; PHP/cURL examples provided.
notes: Data model exposed = brands > promotions > entries/points/winners. No endpoints to create or configure promotions, no rules constructs, no decision endpoints. Paths are unversioned.

claim: The API documentation contains no rate limits, no API versioning scheme, no idempotency guidance, no sandbox/test environment, and no error-code catalog beyond auth failures; recommended testing approach is Postman against the live account.
notes: Absence claim based on full read of the single-page API doc; corroborated by deprecated readme.io docs which also lack these.

claim: Native webhooks exist (Business plan+) but fire on a single event type only — user submits an entry — as a POST with a JSON payload of entry data (email, name, address, birthday, timestamp, IP, promotion id/title, custom fields); delivery is a single attempt with no retry ('If your endpoint is down or returns an error, the data will not be resent') and no signature/HMAC verification is documented.
notes: No winner-drawn, campaign-lifecycle, or validation-status webhook events documented.

claim: Geo Targeting (Business plan+) restricts promotion visibility/entry by country, state, or province using IP-based location; blocked visitors see 'Sorry, this promotion is not available in your location'; misidentified users are handled by manually adding their IP to an Allow IP Addresses list; on purchase promotions only country-level limiting is available.
notes: Doc acknowledges IP/ISP misattribution ('it is likely that their IP Address or ISP is showing as from a different location'). No VPN/proxy detection documented; remedy is a manual allowlist — indicates basic IP geolocation, not compliance-grade geolocation.

claim: Entry fraud controls are a spam filter (default 'high' = 1 entry per IP address), ViralSweep-maintained internal blacklists of known spam IPs/emails auto-marked invalid, an Invalid entries tab with manual re-validation under a status column, an 'events mode' to avoid flagging co-located legitimate entrants, and invalid entries excluded from SMS sends.
notes: No numeric fraud scoring, no device fingerprinting, no reason-code taxonomy documented — signals are IP/email lists and per-IP thresholds.

claim: Instant Win supports three mechanics — randomized odds per prize, seeded/randomly generated win times awarded first-come, and pre-determined winning codes — with unlimited prizes/quantities incl. coupon prizes, a re-entry timer, bonus chances for social actions, and automated winner/non-winner emails.
notes: Mechanics described on official product page; no odds-audit or prize-liability compliance features mentioned.

claim: Winner drawing is dashboard-initiated: choose number of winners and a date range (enabling daily/weekly draws), toggle repeat winners, selection is a 'weighted random process' where each entry is one chance; suspicious winners get an orange caution label (e.g., multiple entries from same IP) and can be deleted/redrawn; winners are NOT auto-notified ('ViralSweep does not notify winners—you'll need to reach out yourself'); winner lists export to CSV.
notes: No third-party certification of drawings, no drawing audit record, no RNG documentation beyond 'weighted random process'.

claim: Live Draws lets customers stream drawings on social media with a fixed 10-second countdown; documentation describes no recording, certification, or randomness-transparency mechanism.
notes: Engagement feature, not an audited-drawing compliance feature.

claim: The free Sweepstakes Rules Generator takes title/URL, eligibility (countries, optional states/provinces, age 13+/18+/21+), sponsor info, prizes/ARV, dates/timezone and outputs official-rules text (copy or .txt download); it is template-based, 'mainly for sweepstakes in the United States and Canada', and carries the disclaimer 'Viralsweep assumes no responsibility for whether you are in compliance with the law' with users acknowledging legal responsibility.
notes: No state registration/bonding threshold logic, no legal-source citations, no lawyer review included in the free tool.

claim: The in-builder official rules template states 'ViralSweep does not guarantee that your promotion complies with local laws' and 'You are responsible for ensuring your official rules meet all legal requirements in your jurisdiction'; the recommended workflow is generate → copy → 'Submit to your legal team for review before launch'; ViralSweep's legal team offers paid custom rule-drafting services (pricing on request).
page_title: Using ViralSweep's Official Rules Template | ViralSweep Support Center
notes: Counsel review is an out-of-band manual step; no in-product approval workflow, rules versioning, or jurisdiction customization documented.

claim: ViralSweep sells full-service sweepstakes management: drafting Official Rules from client-supplied prize/structure info; 'We'll ensure your promotion complies with the law... and provide advice on the proper way to run your promotion'; state registration and bonding handled ('Leave it up to us'); random drawings/judging/voting administration with winner eligibility verification and notification; affidavits for prizes over $600; 1099 IRS forms issued to U.S. winners over $600; prize fulfillment (ship products, send prize money, book trips); AMOE collection via online form or mail-in entries at their PO box; typical turnaround 'within a couple of days'.
notes: This is a human managed service, not product functionality. Page shows client logos incl. UNIQLO, Dermalogica, Crutchfield, Georgia Lottery. Tension with T&C disclaimer of legal advice (VIRALSWEEP-017).

claim: The Enterprise tier (contact sales) lists exactly four differentiators: 'Custom Design/Integrations', 'Legal Administration', 'Bonding & Registrations', and 'Security Assessments'.
page_title: Plans and Pricing (7-Day Free Trial) | Viralsweep
notes: 'Security Assessments' implies willingness to undergo customer security review; no SLA, SSO, or certification commitments published.

claim: Terms & Conditions (operated by 'Clearer'): 'Clearer is solely an online provider of tools and hosting services... We do not provide any legal advice' and 'YOU SHOULD ALWAYS SEEK ADVICE AND INFORMATION FROM A QUALIFIED LEGAL PROFESSIONAL BEFORE OPERATING A PROMOTION'; customers warrant their promotion complies with all applicable State and Federal laws; service is provided AS IS with no SLA/uptime commitment; aggregate liability capped at 12 months of fees; prohibited uses include gambling, illegal lotteries, cryptocurrency promotions, and affiliate/CPA offers.
notes: Legal responsibility sits entirely with the customer; regulated verticals (gambling) are excluded rather than supported. Confirms Clearer (Clearer.io) as operating entity.

claim: GDPR measures (published 2018): Privacy Shield certification, appointed DPO and EU representative, DPAs available; product features include standalone explicit-consent checkboxes ('explicit consent must be presented as a standalone item'), consent records stored with campaign data, per-email search/export for access requests, segment-based deletion across campaigns, deletion within 30 days (immediate on request).
page_title: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) - ViralSweep
notes: Page is dated (May 2018, Privacy Shield since invalidated by Schrems II); explicitly 'not intended to be legal advice'. Confidence reduced for currency.

claim: Every 180 days ViralSweep automatically and irreversibly purges invalid entries (spam-flagged, bot, and 'entries created for testing purposes'); users cannot control or trigger the purge, and purged entries 'cannot be recovered or accessed from your dashboard'.
notes: Retention is fixed policy, not customer-configurable — a problem for evidence retention of fraud/abuse determinations. Also documents that 'test entries' live in production campaigns (no sandbox).

claim: User management has exactly two roles — View Only (view/export campaign data) and Editor (edit campaigns, view/export) — scoped per brand; 'Users added through the Settings tab will have access to all promotions within the brand, not specific ones'; user counts are plan-capped (0/2/4/6 additional users); invited users create individual ViralSweep accounts; SSO is not mentioned.
notes: No promotion-level permissions, no custom roles, no SAML/SSO in official docs.

claim: Multi-brand management is built in: accounts manage 1 (Starter), 2 (Business), 4 (Premium), or 6 (Elite) brands, with per-brand user invitations and brand-scoped campaigns; agencies are an explicit audience ('host partner sweepstakes' on Business+).
page_title: Plans and Pricing (7-Day Free Trial) | Viralsweep
notes: Corroborated by Manage Brands and Additional Users support articles.

claim: The form builder offers: email, name, phone (country codes), Birthday ('Collect birth dates and set a minimum age'), US-only address autocomplete plus full address fields, consent/compliance fields (Agree to Rules, Newsletter/SMS subscribe, GDPR Disclaimer, Disclaimer), Google reCAPTCHA and ViralSweep Captcha, Entry Code, Stripe payments, Signature, custom text/dropdown/radio/checkbox fields, required/optional controls, unlimited fields.
page_title: Custom Form Fields | ViralSweep Support Center
notes: Age gating is self-attested birthday with minimum-age enforcement at the form; no document/ID-based age or identity verification exists.

claim: Verification Codes (Business plan+) implement email-possession verification: after form submission the entrant receives an emailed code that must be entered to finalize the entry — 'a great way to combat users using fake email addresses to enter campaigns'.
notes: This is the only identity-adjacent verification in the product; no KYC, document, phone, or third-party identity verification documented.

claim: Custom Actions (Business plan+) award bonus entries when users complete arbitrary tasks on the customer's website (signups, non-Shopify purchases, form submits, clicks, page visits), verified via two JavaScript tracking scripts (site-wide head script + completion-page script); no API-based or server-side event verification is documented, and Shopify checkout purchase tracking via this method 'is currently not possible'.
notes: Client-side JS verification is spoofable; server-side alternative is the POST /api/points endpoint (Premium+).

claim: The Purchases App runs purchase-based sweepstakes on Shopify/BigCommerce: entries are automatically awarded per dollar spent (e.g., 1 entry per $1) at order placement, 'may take a few minutes to appear in your entrants list'; monthly unique-order caps by plan: 100 (Starter), 1,000 (Business), 5,000 (Premium), unlimited (Elite).
page_title: Shopify Purchase Promotions Setup | ViralSweep Support Center
notes: Asynchronous batch-style ingestion (minutes), not real-time decisioning. Purchase entries link commerce events to promotion entries — nearest thing to promotion-linked value tracking.

claim: Receipt-required sweepstakes collect proof of purchase via a File Upload field on the entry form (1 file on Starter, multiple on Business+; one upload field per campaign); no automated receipt validation/OCR is documented — validation methodology is unspecified.
page_title: How to Upload a Receipt for Sweepstakes Entry | ViralSweep Support Center
notes: Implies manual review of receipts by the sponsor.

claim: ViralSweep was founded in 2012 by Giancarlo Massaro and Steven Kovar, raised no outside funding (bootstrapped), and operated with a small team (listed 1-10 employees).
page_title: ViralSweep - 2025 Company Profile, Team & Competitors - Tracxn
notes: Corroborated by Crunchbase (no funding recorded) and founder profiles. HQ listed as New York by Tracxn/Crunchbase but Boston, MA on the Shopify listing (VIRALSWEEP-029).

claim: ViralSweep was acquired by AppHub in November 2021; AppHub rebranded as Clearer.io, an e-commerce app family whose portfolio includes REVIEWS.io, Influence.io, Boost, Address Validator, Rich Returns, and ViralSweep.
page_title: Clearer.io: A Unified Vision for Smarter eCommerce - ViralSweep
notes: Acquisition date/details corroborated by third-party partner pages (AppHub raised $60M+). Positions ViralSweep inside an SMB e-commerce app rollup, not an enterprise compliance vendor. Sibling app Address Validator is not documented as integrated into ViralSweep entry flows.

claim: The ViralSweep Shopify app (launched August 21, 2013; developer HQ Boston, MA) holds a 4.4/5 rating across 141 reviews (94% 5-star); reviews praise ease of use and support; at least one 1-star review cites unexpected billing on archive mode.
page_title: ViralSweep Giveaways Contests - Shopify App Store
notes: Marketplace listing data; demonstrates a self-serve SMB motion.

claim: ViralSweep advertises enterprise-brand usage via 'trusted by' logos: Purple, Crutchfield, Refinery29, Dermalogica, UNIQLO, Georgia Lottery, TaylorMade, Kendra Scott, Minted, Wix and others.
notes: Logo-wall evidence only; no enterprise case studies or named enterprise references with workflow detail. Georgia Lottery is notable as a regulated entity using them (scope of use unknown).

claim: Published case studies are SMB/mid-market e-commerce (FlySafair, Bruce Lee estate, JewelScent, LostGolfBalls.com, EVELO, Prime Driven) with list-growth and revenue outcomes; no Fortune 500 or regulated-industry case study is published.
notes: Results claims like '150,000 entries and 30,000 ticket sales' (FlySafair) are vendor-reported.

claim: ViralSweep currently publishes no security/trust page: the previously indexed viralsweep.com/security URL now serves the marketing homepage with zero security content (no SOC 2, ISO, PCI, encryption, backup, or pen-test statements anywhere on the current official site).
page_title: Data Security - Viralsweep (URL now renders homepage)
notes: Verified by two fetches (with and without trailing slash) on 2026-08-18; both returned homepage content. Historical aggregator captures describe AWS hosting, encryption, Cloudflare, 2FA, daily encrypted backups, 30-day post-cancellation deletion.

claim: A third-party security aggregator (Nudge Security) lists ViralSweep as SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI, HIPAA, GDPR, FedRamp, and CSA Star Level 1 compliant with Okta SWA/Google/Microsoft login and no 2FA — an implausible combination (e.g., FedRAMP for a giveaway SaaS) that conflicts with the absence of any certification claims on ViralSweep's own site.
notes: Treated as unreliable auto-generated data; used only to flag the unresolved security-certification question. Okta SWA is password vaulting, not SAML SSO.

claim: Competitor Sweeppea's comparison grid credits ViralSweep with managed 1099-MISC forms, NY/FL bonding 'as add-on/service', whitelabeling, and advanced Shopify purchase-to-enter, while claiming ViralSweep lacks an independent third-party administrator for drawings, built-in AMOE management, alcohol (ABC) review expertise, and compliance-vetted legal drafting; it positions ViralSweep as best for 'Agencies & E-comm' lead-gen/referrals.
page_title: Comparison: Sweeppea vs Woobox vs ShortStack vs ViralSweep
notes: Competitor marketing — directionally consistent with ViralSweep's own docs but self-serving; used only as corroboration of positioning, not as proof of absences.

claim: ViralSweep offers a Zapier integration exposing an 'entry is received' trigger that can route entry data to thousands of apps (incl. Webhooks by Zapier), the primary no-code event-out path besides native entry webhooks.
page_title: ViralSweep Integrations | Connect Your Apps with Zapier
notes: Marketplace-documented; official Zapier page exists at viralsweep.com/integrations/zapier/.

claim: The support center's Features collection enumerates the product's full feature surface in 58 articles (white label, API, custom actions, brands, segments, entry limit/codes/frequency, spam filter, geo targeting, GDPR, live draws, draw winners, editing entries, entry purging, events mode, A/B testing, verification codes, coupon codes, languages, payments, receipts, etc.); the enumeration contains NO articles on SSO/SAML, sandbox/staging environments, approval workflows, audit logs, decision/rules engines, policy versioning, case management, or webhook retries.
notes: Used as positive evidence of feature-set scope for reasoned 0 scores (per brief). 'Editing Entries' article confirms entrant records are mutable post-hoc.

claim: ViralSweep's AMOE guidance states 'ViralSweep makes it easy to offer multiple alternative methods of entry' (mail-in, online form, social, phone, in-person are discussed generically), but no product documentation details dedicated AMOE tooling such as mail-in entry digitization or AMOE/paid-entry pool merging; mail-in AMOE collection exists only as the managed-service PO box offering.
page_title: Understanding Sweepstakes Alternate Method of Entry | ViralSweep
notes: Product-side AMOE = free online entry form; service-side = PO box collection (VIRALSWEEP-015).

claim: The legacy developer docs at viralsweep.readme.io are marked 'This documentation has been depreciated. Please visit https://support.viralsweep.com/'; the readme instance contains setup and ESP-integration guides but no OpenAPI endpoint reference in its index.
notes: Developer-docs investment is minimal; the single-page viralsweep.com/api doc is the canonical API reference.

claim: ViralSweep publishes an educational state-by-state sweepstakes-law blog series (e.g., 'Sweepstakes Laws In Virginia', 'Sweepstakes Laws In Alabama' noting 19+ age, international best-practices, registration guides) — content marketing, not a maintained machine-readable legal library or monitoring product.
notes: Verified via search snippets of multiple state-law posts; demonstrates domain knowledge that stays in prose form.

claim: Legacy winner-drawing docs confirm automatic draw of the configured number of winners at campaign end, a red 'FRAUD DETECTION: Draw another winner' prompt when a flagged entrant is drawn, manual Redraw links, winner email + IP address provided to the sponsor, CSV winner export, and explicit statement that 'ViralSweep does not contact your winners for you'.
notes: Deprecated docs; consistent with current Draw Winners article (VIRALSWEEP-011).

claim: ViralSweep competes in a crowded SaaS giveaway-tool segment: Gleam (from ~$79/mo annual), SweepWidget (from ~$25/mo, 90+ entry methods), Woobox (contests/polls/quizzes with enterprise plans), Rafflecopter, and Vyper are recurring head-to-head alternatives; ViralSweep is frequently ranked a top Gleam alternative and differentiates on unlimited entries, A/B testing, API access, and built-for-you promotions.
notes: Corroborated by viral-loops.com Gleam-alternatives roundup, alternativeto.net, and ViralSweep's own viralsweep-vs-gleam comparison post.
